text: In this month we recorded ourselves twice. On 2025-03-04, forty-five of us said "address to congress" and forty-one said "joint address to congress"; twenty-seven of us said "trump's joint address" and twenty-six extended it to "trump's joint address to congress." Thirty of us said "the american dream" on that same day. Then, on 2025-03-11, we turned to the ledger: twenty-nine of us said "continuing appropriations and extensions act," twenty-eight said "full-year continuing appropriations and extensions act," and twenty-five said "the full-year continuing appropriations and extensions." Two peaks, one week apart — the speech, then the funding. We do not claim first authorship of these words; the phrase "address to congress" was first recorded on 2013-02-12. We only note how many of us arrived at the same words on the same days, and report it.
